clis.advanced.asks.desc.defaultMessage: What its screen shows when it asks you something: the agent waits for you, and nothing is typed into it meanwhile. Wrong, a question could be answered by what Combwork types.
clis.advanced.asks.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Screen: asks you something" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description).

clis.advanced.asks.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.advanced.osc7501.desc.defaultMessage: The terminal sequence it writes its turn’s state in (OSC 7501), its first group the state (working, idle). Wrong, its status is read from its screen alone.
clis.advanced.osc7501.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Terminal: its turn’s state" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description). Keep OSC 7501, working and idle as they are.

clis.advanced.osc7501.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.advanced.ready.desc.defaultMessage: What its screen shows when it is ready for a line: Combwork types the first prompt then, and shows it ready. Wrong, it shows as working and nothing is typed into it.
clis.advanced.ready.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Screen: ready for a line" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description).

clis.advanced.ready.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.advanced.titleAsks.desc.defaultMessage: What its terminal title says when it asks you something. Wrong, the agent doesn’t show as waiting for you when it does.
clis.advanced.titleAsks.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Title: asks you something" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description).

clis.advanced.titleAsks.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.advanced.version.desc.defaultMessage: Where its version is in what its version command prints: the first group. Wrong, Provider Setup shows no version.
clis.advanced.version.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Its version" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description).

clis.advanced.version.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.advanced.working.desc.defaultMessage: What its screen shows while it works on a turn. Wrong, Combwork may show it idle while it works, or the other way round.
clis.advanced.working.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Screen: working" is for (Settings → Advanced, a CLI that runs from a description).

clis.advanced.working.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under a CLI that runs from a description, HI-3196).

clis.gaps.heading.defaultMessage: {cli} runs from a description, so it has:
clis.gaps.heading.description: Provider Setup (HI-3196): the heading over the list of what a CLI that runs from a description lacks. {cli} is its name.

clis.gaps.line.description: A note in Agent Settings (HI-3196) about an agent whose CLI runs from a description: what it lacks. {cli} is its name; {gaps} a list of what it lacks.

clis.note.extension.description: Provider Setup, for a CLI that runs from a description: editor extensions are never looked for.

clis.note.install.defaultMessage: It runs from a description in your Combwork folder (clis): install it yourself, then Reload in Settings → Providers → Your own CLIs.
clis.note.install.description: Provider Setup, under a CLI that runs from a description (HI-3196): how it is installed. clis is a folder’s name: keep it. Names of Combwork’s settings: keep them as Combwork shows them.

clis.note.modelPlaceholder.description: The custom model ID box’s placeholder for a CLI that runs from a description without its own example.

clis.note.signIn.defaultMessage: Sign it in as its own documentation says, in a terminal: Combwork runs no sign-in for it.
clis.note.signIn.description: For a CLI that runs from a description (HI-3196): how to sign it in again, Combwork having no sign-in task for it.

clis.problem.badApi.description: Why a CLI description is refused (HI-3197): its server section names a protocol Combwork doesn’t know. Keep server.api, openai and anthropic as they are.

clis.problem.badEnv.defaultMessage: “launch.env” can’t set {name}: {why, select, name {it isn’t a variable’s name} combwork {Combwork’s own variables (CW_…) are Combwork’s} other {}}.
clis.problem.badEnv.description: Why a CLI description is refused: it sets an environment variable it may not. {name} is the variable’s name (keep it).

clis.problem.badId.defaultMessage: “id” must be lower case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter (2 to 31 characters).
clis.problem.badId.description: Why a CLI description is refused: its "id" field (keep it as it is) isn’t a short slug.

clis.problem.badMode.defaultMessage: “launch.modes” has a mode {value} that isn’t a short lower-case name, or is given twice.
clis.problem.badMode.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a permission mode’s "value" (keep the field names) is invalid or repeated. {value} is the value.

clis.problem.badPattern.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a pattern in it doesn’t compile. {field} is its name as written in the file (keep it); {error} the English reason.

clis.problem.badPlaceholder.description: Why a CLI description is refused: an argument names a placeholder Combwork doesn’t fill. {field} is its name as written in the file; {name} the placeholder ({x}); {known} the ones it fills. Keep them as they are.

clis.problem.badType.defaultMessage: “{field}” must be {kind, select, text {text} list {a list of texts} object {an object} yesNo {true or false} other {{kind}}}.
clis.problem.badType.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a field has the wrong kind of value. {field} is its name as written in the file (keep it).

clis.problem.duplicate.defaultMessage: Its id {id} is also in {other}: neither is used.
clis.problem.duplicate.description: Why a CLI description file is refused (HI-3196): another file in the clis folder has the same id. {id} is the id; {other} the other file’s name.

clis.problem.fileBadJson.description: Why a CLI description file is refused (HI-3196): it can’t be read as JSON. {error} is the parser’s English message.

clis.problem.fileTooBig.defaultMessage: It is larger than {max, number} bytes.
clis.problem.fileTooBig.description: Why a CLI description file is refused (HI-3196): it is too large. {max} is the limit in bytes.

clis.problem.idTaken.description: Why a CLI description is refused: another provider or another description has the same id. {id} is the id; {by} names what has it (a provider’s name, or a file).

clis.problem.keyInArgs.defaultMessage: “server.args” can’t name '{key}': a key goes in a variable, never on a command line others can see.
clis.problem.keyInArgs.description: Why a CLI description is refused (HI-3197): it puts the server key in a command-line argument. Keep server.args and {key} as they are.

clis.problem.missing.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a required field is missing. {field} is its name, as written in the file (keep it).

clis.problem.noBaseUrl.defaultMessage: “server” must name '{baseUrl}' in a variable or an argument.
clis.problem.noBaseUrl.description: Why a CLI description is refused (HI-3197): its server section never passes the server’s address. Keep server and {baseUrl} as they are.

clis.problem.noId.description: Why a CLI description is refused: its session arguments (new or resume) don’t name the session id placeholder. Keep "session" and {id} as they are; {which} is new or resume.

clis.problem.noPrompt.defaultMessage: “launch.prompt” must be 'typed', or an object whose 'arg' names '{prompt}'.
clis.problem.noPrompt.description: Why a CLI description is refused: how its first prompt goes in isn’t one of the two forms. Keep "typed", "arg" and {prompt} as they are.

clis.problem.notObject.defaultMessage: It isn’t a description: a JSON object is expected.
clis.problem.notObject.description: Why a CLI description (a JSON file in Combwork’s clis folder, HI-3196) is refused: the file holds something other than a JSON object.

clis.problem.tooLong.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a text in it is too long. {field} is its name as written in the file (keep it); {max} the limit.

clis.problem.tooMany.description: Why a CLI description is refused: a list in it is too long. {field} is its name as written in the file (keep it); {max} the limit.

clis.problem.tooManyFiles.defaultMessage: Only the first {max, number} descriptions are read: this one is left out.
clis.problem.tooManyFiles.description: Why a CLI description file is left out (HI-3196): the clis folder holds more files than Combwork reads.

clis.problem.unreadable.description: Why a CLI description file is refused (HI-3196): reading it failed. {error} is the English reason.

clis.readiness.notFound.defaultMessage: {provider} isn’t found: install it yourself (its description names where it is looked for), then choose Check again.
clis.readiness.notFound.description: Provider Setup, for a CLI that runs from a description (HI-3196): its executable wasn’t found. Combwork has no install task for it.

clis.settings.heading.description: Settings → Providers (HI-3196): the heading over the CLIs that run from a description (a JSON file each in Combwork’s clis folder).

clis.settings.lastGood.defaultMessage: {file} has a problem; its last good version stays in use until it is fixed:
clis.settings.lastGood.description: Settings → Providers (HI-3196): a description file changed into one that can’t be used, while its earlier version is still used for this run. {file} is its name.

clis.settings.none.description: Settings → Providers (HI-3196): the clis folder holds no descriptions.

clis.settings.notUsed.description: Settings → Providers (HI-3196): before the reasons a description file was refused. {file} is its name.

clis.settings.open.description: Button in Settings → Providers (HI-3196): opens the clis folder in Explorer.

clis.settings.reload.description: Button in Settings → Providers (HI-3196): reads the clis folder’s descriptions again.

clis.settings.reloaded.defaultMessage: {n, plural, =0 {No CLIs from descriptions} one {# CLI from a description} other {# CLIs from descriptions}}{problems, plural, =0 {} one {; # description not used} other {; # descriptions not used}}
clis.settings.reloaded.description: A notice after Reload (HI-3196): how many CLIs run from descriptions now, and how many description files couldn’t be used.

clis.settings.what.defaultMessage: A CLI with no provider of its own runs from a description: a JSON file in the clis folder of your Combwork profile. Combwork reads its status from its screen, and never changes its own config.
clis.settings.what.description: Settings → Providers (HI-3196): what the CLIs that run from a description are. clis is a folder’s name: keep it.
